Can I keep using spreadsheets for Making Tax Digital? Bridging software and the digital links rules

By Daniel Wyatt · Facts checked 20 November 2026

Short answer: yes, you can keep your spreadsheet. GOV.UK says a spreadsheet can stay your record-keeping tool, but it can't send anything to HMRC on its own. You need HMRC-recognised software that connects to it, often called bridging software, to send your quarterly updates and submit your tax return. The main thing to check: HMRC lists only 59 of 83 bridging products as able to submit the tax return as well as the quarterly updates.

GOV.UK pages read on 20 November 2026, linked under each section. Product facts come from HMRC's software finder (read 18 November 2026) and providers' own websites. This page sets out the options; it doesn't say which to choose.

Your options if you use spreadsheets

OptionRecords kept inQuarterly updates sent byTax return sent by
Spreadsheet + bridging software that does bothYour spreadsheetBridging softwareThe same bridging software
Spreadsheet + updates-only bridging software + a second productYour spreadsheetBridging softwareA different MTD product, or an agent
Move to all-in-one softwareThe software (bank feed, receipt scanning or manual entry)The same softwareThe same software (GOV.UK says these "will usually" do both)

GOV.UK says you can use more than one product, but only one product for each separate submission. For example, a landlord can't use two products to send the same property update. Whatever mix you use has to cover your income sources, your other income on the tax return, and your update periods (standard or calendar).

Compare all 83 bridging products Bridging that files the tax return too

Sources: GOV.UK, Choose the right software; GOV.UK, Using MTD for Income Tax for the first time; HMRC software finder.

The digital links rule, in plain English

If your records are in one product (your spreadsheet) and submissions go from another (bridging software), GOV.UK says the two must be digitally linked. You set this up when you start, or before you send an update or your tax return.

GOV.UK lists as a digital linkGOV.UK says you must not do
  • Linked cells or formulas in a spreadsheet
  • Emailing a spreadsheet so it can be imported into other software
  • Moving files on a memory stick for someone to import
  • XML or CSV import and export, downloading and uploading files
  • Automated data transfer or an API
  • Copy information by writing it out in another cell or other software
  • Use cut and paste, or copy and paste, to move records

GOV.UK says this applies once a digital record has been sent to HMRC in a quarterly update.

GOV.UK says you don't need to link:

  • other income that isn't self-employment or property, such as dividends or savings
  • software that doesn't create your self-employment or property records, such as a booking system or till
  • a product used only for the tax return; GOV.UK says it gets the data directly from HMRC
  • your records to a co-owner's, if you let a property jointly (see our jointly owned property guide)

If you use one product for everything, GOV.UK says there's nothing to link.

Source: GOV.UK, Create digital records.

What your spreadsheet needs to hold

  • Each record: the amount, the date, and a category. GOV.UK says MTD uses the same income and expense categories as Self Assessment.
  • Less detail if turnover is under £90,000: GOV.UK says sole traders below that level for a business only need to record whether each item is income or an expense. Landlords with residential property also need to mark expenses that are restricted finance costs.
  • One UK property business: all your UK lets count as one business, so one set of records is enough. Each sole trader business needs its own records and its own quarterly updates.
  • When: records for a quarter need to exist before you send that update or before its deadline, whichever comes first. GOV.UK suggests recording things as close to the date as possible.
  • Keep the paperwork: you still keep original records such as bank statements and invoices, and keep digital records for at least 5 years after the 31 January deadline for the tax year.

Quarterly updates are totals per category, not individual transactions. HMRC says it doesn't receive details of individual receipts or invoices. Dates and what goes in an update are on Do I need MTD?

Sources: GOV.UK, Create digital records; GOV.UK, Send quarterly updates.

Fixing a mistake

GOV.UK says to correct the record in your spreadsheet, then digitally link your records to your bridging software again. During the year, the fix flows into your next quarterly update. In HMRC's own myth-buster ahead of the 7 November 2026 deadline, it says there's "no need to resend quarterly updates". If you've already sent the fourth update, GOV.UK gives two routes: correct the record and resend the fourth update, or adjust the category total in your software and reflect it in your records.

Sources: GOV.UK, Create digital records; HMRC press release, 2 November 2026.

What to compare between bridging products

  • Tax return or updates only. 59 of 83 bridging products list both on HMRC's finder.
  • Your spreadsheet. Excel, Google Sheets or a CSV upload: support varies, so check the provider's site.
  • Income types. Self-employment, UK property, foreign property (overseas lettings are a separate business under MTD; see MTD and foreign property).
  • How it's priced. Per year, per month, per submission or per taxpayer. HMRC lists 25 bridging products with a free version (see free MTD software and the catches).
  • Update periods. Standard (tax year) or calendar quarters, if your accounts run to 31 March. See standard vs calendar update periods.

Quick answers

Can I still use a spreadsheet for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax?

Yes. GOV.UK says that if you use spreadsheets for your records you can continue to use them, but you'll still need software that links to your spreadsheets (sometimes called bridging software) to send quarterly updates and submit your tax return.

What is bridging software?

GOV.UK describes it as software that connects to existing records kept in spreadsheets or other accounting tools and makes your submissions to HMRC. HMRC's software finder lists 83 of 179 products for sole traders and landlords as bridging software.

Does all bridging software submit the tax return?

No. GOV.UK says some bridging products let you send quarterly updates and submit your tax return. HMRC's listing shows 59 of the 83 bridging products doing both; the other 24 list quarterly updates only, so a second product (or an agent) would be needed for the tax return.

Can I copy and paste figures from my spreadsheet into MTD software?

GOV.UK says records must be digitally linked when you use more than one product, and gives copying information by writing it out, and cut and paste or copy and paste, as examples of what you must not do once a record has been sent in a quarterly update. Linked cells, CSV or file import and export, and API transfers are among the ways it lists as digital links.

Do I need a separate spreadsheet for each rental property?

GOV.UK says all your UK properties are treated as one UK property business, so you don't need separate digital records for each UK property. Foreign property is different: GOV.UK says to create separate records for each foreign property, which are then added together in one update.

What if I spot a mistake after sending a quarterly update?

GOV.UK says to correct it in your spreadsheet as soon as possible and digitally link your records to your bridging software again. The correction is included in your next quarterly update. HMRC says there's no need to resend the earlier update.
